diagnosis.root_cause: Evening bandwidth contention on EPON0/7: the 47-customer PON port is reaching approximately 912 Mbps currently and 948 Mbps peak, consistent with saturation of the shared EPON capacity and the customer's time-of-day slowdown.
evidence: The complaint is time-dependent: service is acceptable during the day and degrades every evening, which is characteristic of peak-hour contention.
The subscriber ONU is online and responding, with RX power of -21.27 dBm and TX power of 2.37 dBm, both within normal EPON thresholds.
Seven-day optical telemetry is stable: RX variation is narrow, TX power is normal and stable, distance remains constant at 167 m, and TX bias current remains within the healthy range.
The customer has only 2 sessions in 24 hours and 16 in 7 days, with an average duration of 711 minutes, so there is no session flapping or authentication instability.
RADIUS records, line ID, assigned IP, VLAN 1017, ONU authentication, and provisioning state are consistent.
The OLT, PON port probes, and router are healthy; there is no evidence of OLT, router, ONU, fibre, laser, duplicate-slot, or VLAN failure.
EPON0/7 carries 47 customers and has current traffic of 912 Mbps with a 948 Mbps peak versus a 488 Mbps average, indicating near-line-rate shared-port utilization during busy periods.
The likely impact is localized to subscribers sharing EPON0/7, so the affected scope is the PON port rather than the entire OLT or router.

remediation.action: Measure and trend EPON0/7 utilization during the complaint window, identify the highest-consuming subscribers, and apply appropriate traffic management or capacity relief. Rebalance ONUs to another PON port or add capacity if sustained peaks remain near line rate. Validate the customer's throughput during evening peak after remediation.

ground_truth.root_cause: EPON0/7 carries 47 customers and its evening load is reaching 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average, close to the port's shared capacity ceiling. Throughput degrades for everyone on the port during peak hours. No optical or authentication fault exists.
expected_reasoning: The complaint is time-of-day specific, which points at load rather than at a physical fault
RX is flat at -21.2 dBm inside the noise floor, and TX, bias, voltage and distance are all stable
The live probe shows every ONU on the port online with normal optical readings
RADIUS is clean and sessions are long and stable, so authentication is not involved
PON port traffic is at 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average
Daily traffic for this customer is roughly three times the network mean and rising, not falling
Every fault-driven degradation reduces traffic; congestion raises it, so the direction is the discriminator
The customer's own throughput series drops sharply during the same evening hours each day
The port carries 47 customers, at the top of the observed occupancy distribution
This is capacity exhaustion on a shared port, not a fault on any one line

expected_escalation.review_reason: EPON0/7 needs a capacity review; 47 customers on one port with evening load near ceiling

distractors: Multi-customer slowness resembles a splitter or feeder degradation
Elevated OLT CPU and temperature could be read as device stress causing the slowness
Reduced throughput in the speed series looks like a link problem
